reasoning: In March 2016, Google DeepMind's artificial intelligence program AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol, an 18-time world champion and one of the top-ranked Go players in history, in a landmark five-game match by a score of 4 games to 1. Before AlphaGo's rapid rise (including its earlier victory over European champion Fan Hui), computer scientists and Go experts widely believed that a machine beating a top-tier professional human Go player was an achievement at least a decade away, making this milestone significantly ahead of schedule.
